name: Perspectives
description: Viewing direction and foreground context for the existing subjects. Participant viewpoints use someone already in the cast, not an added observer.
entries: head-on view: the main subjects face the viewing position directly
three-quarter rear view: the backs and one side of the subjects are visible together
end-on view: a long shared surface recedes away from the viewing position
view from within a shelf bay: nearby shelf edges frame the activity beyond
window-side view: the view follows the inside face of a window toward the subjects
view from beneath a canopy: the canopy edge occupies the upper foreground above the subjects
view along a corridor: the passage walls recede toward the main action
view from inside an open container: its rim frames the subjects reaching toward its contents
view across water: the intervening water surface separates the viewing position from the subjects
view past a machine: an existing machine occupies one foreground edge without hiding the interaction
view along a railing: the rail recedes from the foreground toward the subjects
reflection-led view: the subjects are primarily visible in an existing reflective surface consistent with its orientation
first-person POV: the view belongs to an existing participant looking toward the interaction, with their visible hands or body establishing their presence when relevant
over-the-shoulder view: part of an existing participant's shoulder occupies one edge, with the other subjects and their interaction visible beyond it
bird's-eye view: the subjects and their surroundings are seen from far above, making their relative positions in the space readable
side view: the main action is seen across the subjects' profiles, with the space between participants visible
three-quarter front view: the view shows the front and one side of the main subjects, revealing depth without a flat head-on arrangement
rear view: the view looks past the backs of the main subjects toward what they are facing
view from across a shared surface: the near edge of the surface leads toward the subjects and the objects they are using
view through an opening: the main subjects remain visible beyond a nearby doorway or gap, with the opening's edges establishing the viewing position
